content: Keep the desktop UI's established look, which the user approved on 2026-10-08. It has a navy brand header (--brand #1f3a5f), a light canvas (#f2f4f7) with white panels, an 8px radius, and Segoe UI text with Cascadia Mono for code. The results list sits on the left (20–26rem) and the part detail on the right. The window itself never scrolls; only panels and columns do. Inside the part detail, a header sits on top. Below it, the symbol and footprint are stacked on the left and share the height, and every catalog field is always visible on the right, with no collapsible. Long URL values stay on one line with an ellipsis. Symbols render on KiCad's light schematic paper and footprints on KiCad's dark board (#001023). Each error state has one alert, and supporting notes stay quiet. Reuse the tokens in apps/desktop-ui/styles.css rather than adding colours, and extend this layout rather than redesigning it.

title: Sign in to the team catalog with an in-memory session, loopback only for now
rationale: The desktop saves only the team server address and email (config/team.json); the password is sent once to auth-with-password and the session token stays in memory, so nothing secret is stored and a restart asks for the password again. Only http://127.0.0.1, localhost or [::1] are accepted because collaboration's realtime client speaks plain HTTP and a password must not cross a network unencrypted; a shared server needs HTTPS realtime first. Edit access is the users field can_edit_catalog, which members cannot set on themselves.

description: A component class with display:flex (.team-tabs) overrode the HTML hidden attribute, so tabs meant to hide behind the conflict view stayed visible; the journey's el.hidden check still passed.
resolution: styles.css ends with [hidden] { display: none !important; }. Journey 06 checks layout (getClientRects().length === 0), not the hidden property.

description: In Leptos 0.8.3, calling .track() on a Memo inside an Effect did not re-run the Effect when the memo's source changed (the search did not refresh after a team Change), while .get() on an equivalent memo elsewhere worked.
resolution: Read the memo's value in the Effect (let _ = memo.get();) instead of only tracking it; .track() is fine on RwSignals (apps/desktop-ui/src/main.rs search effect).

title: The team column shows shared part details and the current revision apart; one Edit part form
rationale:
Seed kicad-parts-7556, chosen for the simplest product without asking the user (who asked for best judgement); revised after review. Wording below is exactly what apps/desktop-ui/src/team.rs and main.rs show.

Revision wording: the part's own revision reads 'revision N of this part' (header Source fact 'Team catalog, revision N of this part'; Details heading 'Symbol and footprint (revision N of this part)'). A CAD item's own revision reads 'symbol revision N' or 'footprint revision N' (binding rows such as 'g-pas:R_US, symbol revision 1', history change rows, preview labels 'team catalog, symbol revision N', fallback notes 'Symbol revision N of <ref> could not be fetched ...'), so the two never read alike. History entries keep 'Revision N · ...', since there it can only be the part's.

Details tab: 'Part details (N)' with the 'Edit part' button (or 'You can view this part but not edit it.'), the hint 'Every revision of the part shares these details.', the fields table, 'Manufacturer parts', then 'Symbol and footprint (revision N of this part)' (or 'This part uses no symbol or footprint.'). That table ends with a read-only 'Excluded from BOM' row (kicad-parts-ccc0): 'Yes: its symbol says it is not in the BOM', 'Yes: every footprint choice says it is not in the BOM', 'No', 'No: only some footprint choices say it is not in the BOM', or 'Not known: the symbol comes from KiCad's own library, which this app does not read yet' (also '... is not in the Catalog'). History rows say 'Yes'/'No'. No separate list of other revisions: the history already lists every revision.

One 'Edit part' form, not two: heading 'Edit part', hint 'Change details only to correct them. A part with a different value, package or pinout needs a new IPN.', fieldsets 'Part details', 'Manufacturer parts (the first is the main one)', and 'Symbol and footprint' with the hint 'Changing these adds a new revision of this part. Designs that use revision N keep it.' When someone else saves meanwhile: 'Someone else saved a change to this part while you were editing. When you save, you can compare your changes with theirs.' Save notices: 'Saved. The part details changed; no revision was added.' or 'Saved as revision N.'

History: one entry per Change, titled 'Part details · Edited by X' or 'Revision N · Imported by an administrator', with the revision's state next to it: 'Revision 1 (current) · Imported by an administrator', 'Revision 2 (archived) · Edited by X'. The selected entry shows 'What changed in revision N' or 'What changed in the part details' with Field/Before/After rows (details rows first); revision 1 says 'The first revision of this part.'

Conflict screen: one heading 'Someone else changed this part first', the line 'X saved a change on <time> ("reason") after you started editing. Your changes are not saved yet.', one table with columns Field / You started from / Theirs / Yours ('not changed' where you changed nothing), the hint 'Saving on top keeps their changes and adds yours. Where you both changed a field, yours is kept.', and buttons 'Save my changes on top of theirs', 'Edit again', 'Discard my changes'. Deliberate simplification: one heading and one table cover both sections, while the behaviour stays per section (only rows of what moved or what you changed appear, and saving on top resends only the sections you changed).

Archive (kicad-parts-5bea): a selected revision entry in History offers 'Archive revision N…' or, when archived, 'Unarchive revision N…' (editors only). It opens a small form 'Archive revision N' with 'KiCad and this app stop offering revision N, so nobody new picks it. Designs that already use it keep it. Nothing is deleted. The current revision becomes (or stays) revision X.' (unarchive: 'KiCad and this app offer revision N again. The current revision becomes (or stays) revision X.'); focus moves to the reason box when the form opens and back to its button on Cancel; if someone else archives or unarchives that revision meanwhile, the form closes with 'Someone else already archived revision N, so nothing was saved.', 'Why are you archiving it?' and a reason. The only revision not archived shows 'Revision N is the only revision that is not archived, so it cannot be archived. Add a corrected revision first.' instead of a button, so the refusal comes before submitting. Notices: 'Revision N is archived. The current revision is now (or stays) revision X.' / 'Revision N is no longer archived. The current revision is now (or stays) revision X.' The 'Revision N · Archived by X' entry also offers 'Unarchive revision N…' while the revision is still archived, so undo is next to what was just done. History entries read 'Revision N · Archived by X' (selected: 'Revision N archived', 'Revision N was archived. The current revision became revision X.'), and revision entries carry '(archived)' or '(current)' right after the revision number. The Details tab ends with 'Other revisions: revision 1 (older), revision 3 (archived).' when there are others. Styles reuse the existing tokens; the new rules are '.archive-form' (the light panel the removed restore form used: #f5f7fa, --line border, --radius), '.archive-open', '.team-toolbar + .hint { margin: 0 0 0.5rem; }' (the line under a section heading) and '.binding { white-space: nowrap; }' (a binding such as 'footprint revision 1' stays on one line, so a long reference breaks after its comma).

New CSV values (kicad-parts-75a5, revised after review): shown only when the CSV changed after the app edit. At the top of the Details tab, a warm notice with role="status" headed 'New values in the CSV' says '<file> has new values for this part. They were not applied, because the part was edited in this app.' with a 'Review CSV values' button (viewers see 'Someone who can edit parts can review them.'). The review form replaces the details (like Edit part): heading 'Review CSV values' (focused), '<file> has new values for this part. Tick the ones to accept. The others stay as they are, and you are not asked about these CSV values again unless the CSV changes.', a table Accept / Field / Now / In the CSV (field names in ink) with one checkbox per row (values the CSV changed first, then values it did not change, marked '(not changed in the CSV)'; nothing pre-ticked; rows leave as their group is saved), for CAD the hint 'Accepting the Symbol or Footprint adds revision N of this part. Designs that use revision M keep it.', the label 'Reason (shown in the history)' prefilled 'Accept CSV values from <file>', and buttons 'Accept the ticked values' (disabled until something is ticked), 'Keep current values' (uses 'Keep the values edited in this app, not the CSV values from <file>' when the prefilled reason is untouched) and 'Cancel'. One word throughout: accept. Notices: 'Saved. The part details changed; no revision was added.', 'Saved as revision N.', both: 'Saved. The part details changed, and the new symbol or footprint is revision N.', kept: 'Kept the current values. You are asked about these CSV values again only if the CSV changes.', all already reviewed: 'These CSV values were already reviewed, so nothing was saved.'; focus returns to 'Part details (N)'. History titles: 'Part details · Accepted CSV values by X' (or 'Revision N · Accepted CSV values') and 'CSV values · Kept current part details by X' / '... Kept current symbol and footprint ...' (heading 'CSV values not accepted').

description: The narrow-window media query (max-width 70rem) that stacks .part-body came before .part-body.team, which has equal-or-higher specificity, so team parts never stacked: at the 960 px minimum width the preview column was about 75 px and the footprint name ran into the fields. Long unbroken words in the part header and manufacturer list also widened the panel.
resolution: Repeat the media query after any later layout rule it must override (styles.css after .part-body.team); wrap header, facts and manufacturer list with overflow-wrap: anywhere. Journey 09 resizes to 960 px with browser.setWindowSize and asserts nothing scrolls sideways (screenshots must stay 1280x800, so assert rather than screenshot).

description: The archive form reused the previous save's correlation ID when the same revision was archived again with the same reason (after someone else unarchived it), so PocketBase replayed the old applied answer and the app claimed a save that never happened.
resolution: Give every opened form a new correlation ID (TeamUi::start_archiving, like start_editing); reuse an ID only for a retry while the same form stays open.

title: Use a file in Edit part: hidden file input, read in the webview, Tauri reads and draws
rationale: Seed kicad-parts-3b8b, product calls by best judgement. Under the Symbol and Footprint fields, a visually hidden <input type=file> (WebDriver addValue sets it) with a label styled as a button ('Use a file…', then 'Use another file…'); its container is position: relative, because a visually hidden (position: absolute) input inside a scrolling column whose containing block is outside it widened and lengthened the whole part panel (outer scrollbars appeared). The webview reads the bytes (File.arrayBuffer through js_sys::Reflect, no new web-sys features), refuses a wrong extension or a file over 24 MB plainly, and sends base64 to team_read_file (catalog-browser TeamCatalog::read_file: names, chosen, library suggestion, missing Catalog 3D models) and team_preview_file (CatalogBrowser::preview_file, drawing the bytes the Catalog would store through PreviewCache::stored_symbol/stored_footprint, so a saved revision with the same bytes is already cached). The field is filled with LIB:NAME (current g- library, else the part's CSV file for symbols, else the package suggestion; no library leaves just NAME with a hint); for a footprint only the first choice is replaced. A symbol library with several symbols shows a select, preselecting the one named like the current reference. Missing Catalog 3D models each get their own file input; leaving one empty saves a missing 3D model. 'Don't use the file' restores the field. Files ride in TeamEditRequest.files (kind, file name, base64, symbol, model key); catalog-browser takes a symbol/footprint file's reference from its field at save time. The saved message adds 'N other parts still use an older revision of the footprint X.' History adds a '<Kind> file' row from the replaced revision's file (import path or chosen file name) to the new one; value_view keeps the reference after ' of ' whole up to its colon.

description: In the Library check view, each 'Add part from it' button carried a .visually-hidden span (position: absolute, 1px, clipped) with the item's reference. The buttons had no positioned ancestor inside the scrolling list, so the hidden spans were placed against the part panel and lengthened it: the panel got a second, outer scrollbar (journey 14 screenshot 62 changed by 6%). Using aria-label instead failed axe's label-content-name-mismatch, because the accessible name must contain the visible text.
resolution: Keep the visible text in the accessible name and add the extra words in a .visually-hidden span inside the control, and give that control position: relative so the hidden span stays inside it (styles.css .library-check-add). Select such buttons in journeys by a data attribute (data-reference), not by aria name.
